name: Forecast generation, availability and fuel needs
summary: Every morning the portfolio optimisation team builds an hourly forecast of what each plant can and is likely to generate over the next week, with a longer monthly view for hedging. They combine weather forecasts, the AESO's central wind forecast, the converted gas units' status from the plants, the hydro water schedule, turbine availability from the renewables control centre and the accepted outage schedule, then derive the gas burn the plants will need. The forecast feeds the day's energy offers, gas buying and hedging, and must match the capability declared to the AESO. It is error-prone because wind and river flows are uncertain, inputs arrive by phone and email from several control rooms, and trips or derates during the day force updates.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator of about 1,300 staff with converted gas units, cogeneration, wind, hydro and a battery, whose portfolio optimisation team sits beside a 24-hour real-time desk.
baseline.notes: The optimisation team took its current form in 2021 when the Alberta power purchase arrangements ended; before that the forecast was simpler because much of the output was dispatched under the arrangements.

trigger: Overnight weather and wind forecasts arrive and the plants report their status for the morning.
end_state: The forecast is published to the offer desk, the gas scheduler and the term traders, updated during the day when needed, and the next morning the day's forecast error is recorded.

volume.seasonality: Every calendar day; weekend forecasts are lighter and done by the real-time desk. Spring runoff and winter wind storms bring more intraday updates.

evidence.note: Optimisation team for the Alberta merchant portfolio in w3; one forecast per day by definition.
Optimisation team in w3; seven analysts in the organisation file also prepare offers and hedge positions.

steps.name: Download weather and AESO wind forecasts
steps.description: Scheduled jobs download the overnight weather model runs for the plant locations and the AESO's central wind and solar forecast into the forecasting tools.

error.defect_description: A download fails and yesterday's run is used.

evidence.note: AESO 7-day-ahead wind forecast updated hourly and 12-hour forecast every 10 minutes (w5); job timing estimated.

steps.name: Pull overnight actuals from historian
steps.description: Scheduled jobs copy the previous day's hourly output, wind speeds, river flows and reservoir levels from the plant historian and SCADA into the forecast workbook.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; assumed.

steps.name: Check data feeds and fill gaps
steps.description: The portfolio optimisation analyst, or the real-time trader at weekends, opens the forecast workbook, checks that every feed updated and looks for missing hours, frozen values or a weather run that did not arrive.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; times estimated.

steps.name: Rebuild missing inputs by hand
steps.description: The analyst downloads the missing forecast from the provider's website or copies values from SCADA screens into the workbook, and logs an IT ticket for the failed job.

error.defect_description: Values pasted into the wrong hours.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; times estimated.

steps.name: Take gas unit status on morning call
steps.description: On the morning call each converted unit's and cogeneration plant's shift supervisor reports current capability, derates, minimum stable load, equipment problems and expected return-to-service times.

error.defect_description: Derate reported in the wrong unit or for the wrong hours.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; morning call assumed.

steps.name: Report wind turbine availability
steps.description: The renewables operations centre operator sends the number of turbines down at each wind farm, expected repair dates, icing and any transmission curtailment, and the battery's state.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; assumed.

steps.name: Send hydro water schedule and constraints
steps.description: The hydro control centre operator sends the day's release plan by river system, minimum flow and reservoir level limits from the water licences, and any plant out of service.

error.defect_description: Schedule sent for the wrong day.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; assumed.

steps.name: Check outage schedule for changes
steps.description: The analyst opens the accepted outage schedule, compares it with yesterday's copy and notes any planned outage that moved, started or was extended.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; times estimated.

steps.name: Forecast wind output by farm
steps.description: The analyst blends the AESO central wind forecast with the company's own weather-based forecast for each wind farm, scales it for turbines out of service and adjusts for icing and curtailment.

evidence.note: AESO central forecast publication in w5; blending method and times estimated.

steps.name: Forecast hydro output
steps.description: The analyst converts the water schedule into hourly MW for each hydro plant using flow-to-power tables, and checks it against reservoir limits and the flexibility kept for price peaks and ancillary services.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; times estimated.

steps.name: Forecast gas unit capability and dispatch
steps.description: The analyst sets each gas unit's hourly capability from the status report and the temperature forecast, and estimates the likely dispatch level from the short-term price view and the units' costs.

error.defect_description: Dispatch assumption inconsistent with the price view.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; times estimated.

steps.name: Give short-term price and load view
steps.description: The market fundamentals analyst sends the expected hourly Alberta load, supply and pool price range for the coming days, flagging hours when tight supply could make prices spike.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; assumed.

steps.name: Assemble hourly portfolio forecast
steps.description: The analyst combines the wind, hydro, gas, cogeneration and battery forecasts into one hourly table for seven days with an expected value and a low and high case, and a monthly view for the rest of the year.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; times estimated.

steps.name: Derive fuel burn by plant
steps.description: The analyst multiplies each gas unit's forecast hourly output by its heat-rate curve and adds start-up gas and the cogeneration hosts' steam load to give GJ per plant per gas day.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; times estimated.

steps.name: Compare with yesterday and actuals
steps.description: The analyst compares today's forecast with yesterday's and with the latest actual output, and explains every change larger than a set threshold before the forecast is used.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; share estimated.

steps.name: Desk lead reviews forecast
steps.description: The real-time desk lead reads the forecast summary, questions large changes in availability or wind, and agrees the numbers the offers will be built on.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; review step assumed.

steps.name: Check declared availability matches forecast
steps.description: The analyst compares each asset's forecast capability with the available capability declared to the AESO in the Energy Trading System and lists any asset whose declaration must be restated.

control.basis: AESO ISO rules section 203.3: available capability restated as soon as reasonably practicable after a change for an acceptable operational reason

evidence.note: Restatement duty in w4; mismatch share estimated.

steps.name: Restate available capability
steps.description: The real-time trader enters the restated available capability and the operational reason for the affected hours in the Energy Trading System.

error.defect_description: Restatement entered for the wrong hours.

control.basis: AESO ISO rules section 203.3: restatement with reasons

evidence.note: Restatement requirements in w4; times estimated.

steps.name: Publish forecast
steps.description: The analyst saves the forecast to the shared folder and reporting site and emails a summary to the offer desk, the gas scheduler and the term traders before the offer and gas trading deadlines.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; times estimated.

steps.name: Update medium-term forecast for hedging
steps.description: Once a week the analyst extends the forecast month by month to the end of the next two years, using the outage plan, normal wind and water, and expected gas dispatch, for the hedge position.

error.defect_description: Outage in the plan missed for a later year.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; weekly cadence estimated.

steps.name: Monitor actuals against forecast
steps.description: Through the day the real-time trader watches actual output, wind ramps and unit alarms against the published forecast and decides whether a change is large enough to reissue it.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; share of days with updates estimated.

steps.name: Issue intraday forecast update
steps.description: The real-time trader updates the affected hours in the forecast, tells the gas scheduler and the offer desk of the change, and notes the cause.

error.defect_description: Update not passed to the gas scheduler.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; times estimated.

steps.name: Record forecast error
steps.description: The next morning the analyst compares the day's forecast with metered output by asset and records the error, so recurring bias in wind, hydro or gas dispatch can be corrected.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common practice for a multi-technology generator's portfolio forecast; times estimated.

exceptions.name: Intraday update
exceptions.description: A unit trip, derate or wind ramp makes the real-time desk reissue part of the forecast.

exceptions.name: Capability restatement
exceptions.description: The forecast shows capability different from the AESO declaration and the desk restates it.

exceptions.name: Feed failure
exceptions.description: A weather or historian feed fails and the analyst rebuilds the input by hand.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from overnight forecast download to recorded forecast error
benchmarks.population: Daily portfolio forecast at an Alberta generator

evidence.note: Follows from the daily timetable: forecast published mid-morning, monitored through the day, error recorded the next morning.

benchmarks.unit: minutes between updates of the AESO 12-hour wind forecast
benchmarks.population: AESO central wind and solar forecast

evidence.note: 7-day-ahead forecast refreshes hourly.

benchmarks.population: TransAlta Alberta merchant portfolio, first year of the optimisation team

pain_points.description: Plant, wind and hydro inputs arrive by phone and email from three control rooms and are re-keyed into a spreadsheet.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of 2019-2022 tooling.

pain_points.description: Wind ramps and unit trips make about two days in five need an intraday update, which must reach the gas scheduler and the offer desk quickly.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Declared AESO capability can drift from the forecast, and a missed restatement is a market rule breach.

evidence.note: Restatement duty in w4.

pain_points.description: Feed failures force manual rebuilding of inputs early in the morning before the offer deadline.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation 2021 Integrated Report (Form 6-K)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: A new team charged with optimising Alberta merchant market performance had its first year in 2021, delivering 864 million CAD of gross margin from hydro, wind, gas, coal and storage; the hedge program focuses on merchant Gas and Energy Transition generation; 75 percent of Gas production sold forward at end 2021 (100 percent at end 2020) at an average hedged power price of 72 CAD/MWh; AECO gas price 3.39 CAD/GJ in 2021. Only the first part of this long document was read.

sources.title: ISO Rules Section 203.3 Energy Restatements (effective 2014-07-02)
sources.supports: A pool participant must submit an available capability restatement as soon as reasonably practicable when capability changes for an acceptable operational reason, with the reason; price and MW restatements only up to two hours before the settlement interval. In force through the 2019 to 2022 period.

sources.title: Wind and Solar Power Forecasting
sources.supports: The AESO publishes a centralised wind and solar power forecast: a 12-hour forecast updated every 10 minutes and a 7-day-ahead forecast updated hourly, downloadable as CSV files.

assumptions: On weekends and holidays the real-time trader runs a lighter version of steps s03 to s19; the step roles show the weekday case.

The morning call inputs (s05 to s07) run in parallel; the simulation adds them in sequence, which slightly overstates the elapsed time; together with sequential hands-on time this puts the simulated median about 0.3 days above the 1.2-day timetable benchmark.
No plant, vehicle or crew is held by forecasting, and no travel, weather wait or site access applies: weather affects the forecast content, not the wait.

Real-time trader, real-time desk lead, gas shift supervisor, renewables operations centre operator and hydro control centre operator take part but are not listed in the organisation file's process roles.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
